blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.

Who looks after the children in today's Britain?

A When Simon Baron-Cohen recently published a book, The Essential Difference, in which he claimed that the female brain is predominantly hard-wired for empathy, the male brain is predominantly hard-wired for understanding and building systems, he caught the mood of the moment. His team's experiments on day-old babies, and the finding that the male babies looked for longer at a hanging toy and the female babies longer at a face, has been repeatedly cited in the press since his book's publication. However, Elizabeth Spelke is one expert who is sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention. This is one isolated experiment, she says. 'Its findings fly in the face of dozens of studies on similar aspects of cognition carried out on young babies over decades. It is astonishing how much this one study has been cited, when the many studies that show no difference between the sexes, or a difference in the other direction, are ignored.'

B One of Baron-Cohen's other main studies was conducted by collecting and examining responses to questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour: the sort of quiz well known to readers of magazines. The answers recorded in such cases will reflect differences formed by cultural assumptions and socialisation: it is hard to see what they tell us about innate differences. Nevertheless, they have become a fashionable reference point, and recently Princess Anne, patron of Women into Science and Engineering, gave a speech in which she quoted Baron-Cohen's research as proof that six out of ten men have a systemising brain. This kind of science has passed into everyday culture, often outrunning the intentions of those who did the original work.

C Social expectations play heavily with young men and women, and expectations are in some ways more conventional in Britain today than they were ten or 20 years ago. It is particularly when they have children that women find out how society reinforces traditional expectations of their behaviour. They discover that many pressures including the work schedule of their male partner and the expectations of his employer that it should be maintained - make it hard to combine work and home without giving their paid work a lower priority than their male colleagues do. In such a context, the claims about males' greater power to systemise and compete only serve to put further pressure on women.

D The pressures are equally powerful on men to continue in a traditional lifestyle. Some educationalists argue that among young men the concern that they might appear 'feminine' is higher than ever and may even hold back educational achievement, since studying is often seen as girlish. In later life, the drive to competitiveness in the workplace is mythologised as being tied to high levels of masculinity. Men are also told that high achievers attract more women, even though evidence shows that as women slowly become more equal at work, they begin to care less about the economic status of potential partners.

E Men are often held back from making the choice to move deeper into domestic life, and in particular childcare, feeling that it lacks status. While the gains in making a social revolution were clear for women - they could gain status and income by moving beyond the home - the gains in the parallel social revolution are harder for men to see, since it will involve them in losing status and income. The idea that men are naturally less empathetic also produces feelings of fatalism about their role. Yet there is much evidence to show that even being empathetic and good at parenting is a learned behaviour.

F It is true that, as the linguist Steven Pinker noted, in our culture women respond more readily to their children's cries, but there is nothing to say that this is down to anything other than practice and socialisation. In a culture where most men return to work straight after the birth of their children, it would be extraordinary if they did manage to remain as alert to their needs as women who remain at home. In one test carried out with teenagers, although girls said that they liked children more than boys said they did, when left alone with a crying infant, their responses were no different. Women can testify to the fact that parenting is a tricky, complicated process, not always a natural, easy role.

G However, while the definite trend of a decade ago is no longer evident, the movement towards equality has not completely stalled. A more equal sharing of childcare and even domestic labour is still desired by many men as well as women. Nearly three-quarters of young British men say that if it were financially possible they would like to stay at home to look after their families. And three-quarters of young men tell pollsters that the amount of time fathers are allowed to take off work after a birth - paternity leave - is too short in Britain. The government is therefore proposing more equal policies on maternity/paternity leave, knowing that the pressure is still forwards rather than backwards. And remember that in Britain, young men in full-time work spend about an hour a day looking after their children. That may sound paltry, but not compared to the 15 minutes they spent 30 years ago: if the time went on increasing fourfold every 30 years, equal partnership would become a reality for their grandchildren.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 27-33

Reading Passage 3 has seven paragraphs, A-G.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A-G, in boxes 27-33 on your answer sheet. You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEFG
27 a possible argument for poor academic performance in young boys
28 a comparison between fathers' and mothers' reactions to babies' demands
29 a reference to a change in women's interest in men's earning power
30 a reference to a study on infant behaviour
31 a prediction that there will be more involvement of men in childcare
32 a reference to analysis using a popular self-assessment method
33 results of an experiment on adolescents' reactions to young babies

Questions 34-36

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

34 What is Elizabeth Spelke's reaction to Baron-Cohen's experiment?

35 According to the writer, why do mothers often put childcare above career demands?

36 What does the writer suggest about women as parents in paragraph F?

Questions 37-40

Complete the summary below.

Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

Men and childcare

One reason why some men may be unwilling to leave their jobs to look after their children is because the gains that could come with such a change are not obvious. Staying at home would in fact mean accepting a considerable drop in pay and in 37 . The conventional notion that men are not as 38 as women may also lead men to experience a certain sense of resignation about their traditional place in society. However, it is interesting to note that the majority of young men in the UK say that the statutory time permitted for 39 is inadequate. Influence is thus being exerted on the 40 to review the existing provision.

items.text:
（1）题目 27：a possible argument for poor academic performance in young boys
题目翻译：年轻男孩学业表现不佳的一个可能原因。
答案：D（Paragraph D）
定位：正文 D 段，前半部分
原文：Some educationalists argue that among young men the concern that they might appear 'feminine' is higher than ever and may even hold back educational achievement, since studying is often seen as girlish.
译文：一些教育工作者认为，年轻男性担心自己显得“女性化”的程度比以往更高，这甚至可能阻碍学业成就，因为学习常被看成女孩子做的事。

解析：题干的 possible argument 对应 Some educationalists argue；poor academic performance 对应 hold back educational achievement。因此信息位于 D 段。

（2）题目 28：a comparison between fathers’ and mothers’ reactions to babies’ demands
题目翻译：父亲和母亲对婴儿需求反应的比较。
答案：F（Paragraph F）
定位：正文 F 段，前半部分
原文：women respond more readily to their children's cries, but there is nothing to say that this is down to anything other than practice and socialisation. In a culture where most men return to work straight after the birth of their children, it would be extraordinary if they did manage to remain as alert to their needs as women who remain at home.
译文：女性对孩子哭声反应得更快，但没有证据表明这不是练习和社会化造成的。在男性通常于孩子出生后立即返工的文化中，如果他们还能像留在家中的女性一样敏锐地察觉孩子需求，反而很不寻常。

解析：fathers’ and mothers’ reactions 对应返工的男性与留在家中的女性之间的比较；babies’ demands 对应 children’s cries 和 their needs。因此选 F。

（3）题目 29：a reference to a change in women’s interest in men’s earning power
题目翻译：提到女性对男性赚钱能力的兴趣发生变化。
答案：D（Paragraph D）
定位：正文 D 段，末句
原文：Men are also told that high achievers attract more women, even though evidence shows that as women slowly become more equal at work, they begin to care less about the economic status of potential partners.
译文：男性也被告知成就越高越能吸引女性；然而证据表明，随着女性在工作中逐渐获得更平等的地位，她们开始不那么在意潜在伴侣的经济地位。

解析：men’s earning power 对应 economic status of potential partners；a change in women’s interest 对应 begin to care less。因此选 D。

（4）题目 30：a reference to a study on infant behaviour
题目翻译：提到一项关于婴儿行为的研究。
答案：A（Paragraph A）
定位：正文 A 段，前半部分
原文：His team's experiments on day-old babies, and the finding that the male babies looked for longer at a hanging toy and the female babies longer at a face, has been repeatedly cited in the press since his book's publication.
译文：他的团队对出生一天的婴儿进行了实验，发现男婴看悬挂玩具的时间更长，女婴看人脸的时间更长；该发现自书出版后被媒体反复引用。

解析：a study on infant behaviour 对应 experiments on day-old babies 以及婴儿注视玩具或人脸的行为。因此选 A。

（5）题目 31：a prediction that there will be more involvement of men in childcare
题目翻译：预测男性会更多参与育儿。
答案：G（Paragraph G）
定位：正文 G 段，末句
原文：if the time went on increasing fourfold every 30 years, equal partnership would become a reality for their grandchildren.
译文：如果男性照顾孩子的时间每30年继续增长四倍，那么平等的育儿伙伴关系将在他们孙辈一代成为现实。

解析：prediction 对应条件句 would become a reality；equal partnership 表明未来男性在育儿中的参与会增加。因此选 G。

（6）题目 32：a reference to analysis using a popular self-assessment method
题目翻译：提到使用一种流行的自我评估方法进行分析。
答案：B（Paragraph B）
定位：正文 B 段，首句
原文：One of Baron-Cohen's other main studies was conducted by collecting and examining responses to questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour: the sort of quiz well known to readers of magazines.
译文：Baron-Cohen 的另一项主要研究通过收集并分析成年人对自身行为问卷的回答进行；这种小测验为杂志读者所熟悉。

解析：analysis 对应 collecting and examining responses；self-assessment method 对应 adults 对自身 behaviour 填写 questionnaires；popular 对应 well known to readers of magazines。因此选 B。

（7）题目 33：results of an experiment on adolescents’ reactions to young babies
题目翻译：一项青少年面对年幼婴儿时反应实验的结果。
答案：F（Paragraph F）
定位：正文 F 段，后半部分
原文：In one test carried out with teenagers, although girls said that they liked children more than boys said they did, when left alone with a crying infant, their responses were no different.
译文：一项针对青少年的测试发现：虽然女孩自称比男孩更喜欢孩子，但当他们被单独留下照看哭泣的婴儿时，反应并无差别。

解析：adolescents 对应 teenagers；young babies 对应 a crying infant；results 对应 their responses were no different。因此选 F。

items.text:
（1）题目 34：What is Elizabeth Spelke’s reaction to Baron-Cohen’s experiment?
题目翻译：Elizabeth Spelke 对 Baron-Cohen 的实验有何反应？
答案：C（She is doubtful whether it merits the notice it has been given.）
定位：正文 A 段，后半部分
原文：However, Elizabeth Spelke is one expert who is sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention.
译文：然而，Elizabeth Spelke 是一位怀疑这项实验是否值得如此关注的专家。

解析：sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention 与 C 项 “doubtful whether it merits the notice it has been given” 完全同义，因此选 C。

（2）题目 35：According to the writer, why do mothers often put childcare above career demands?
题目翻译：作者认为，母亲为什么常把育儿置于职业需求之上？
答案：A（Few allowances are made for fathers to reduce their working hours.）
定位：正文 C 段，中部
原文：They discover that many pressures - including the work schedule of their male partner and the expectations of his employer that it should be maintained - make it hard to combine work and home without giving their paid work a lower priority than their male colleagues do.
译文：她们发现，多种压力——包括男性伴侣的工作安排以及其雇主要求保持该安排——使她们很难兼顾工作与家庭，除非把有偿工作的优先级放得低于男性同事。

解析：题干的 put childcare above career demands 对应 giving their paid work a lower priority。原因是父亲的工作安排被期待保持不变，即很少得到减少工时的灵活安排，所以选 A。

（3）题目 36：What does the writer suggest about women as parents in paragraph F?
题目翻译：作者在 F 段对女性作为父母提出了什么看法？
答案：B（They have to work at mastering the skills of motherhood.）
定位：正文 F 段，末句
原文：Women can testify to the fact that parenting is a tricky, complicated process, not always a natural, easy role.
译文：女性可以证明，育儿是棘手而复杂的过程，并不总是一种自然、轻松的角色。

解析：原文明确定否“女性天生就会育儿”，说明育儿技能需要练习和掌握，对应 B “have to work at mastering the skills of motherhood”。

items.text:
（1）题目 37：One reason why some men may be unwilling to leave their jobs to look after their children is because the gains that could come with such a change are not obvious. Staying at home would in fact mean accepting a considerable drop in pay and in ________. The conventional notion that men are not as ________ as women may also lead men to experience a certain sense of resignation about their traditional place in society.
题目翻译：待在家照顾孩子会使收入和什么大幅下降？
答案：status
定位：正文 E 段，中部
原文：the gains in the parallel social revolution are harder for men to see, since it will involve them in losing status and income.
译文：男性较难看出这场平行社会变革的收益，因为它会使他们失去社会地位和收入。

解析：题干已用 pay 对应 income，另一个并列损失是 status，因此填 status。

（2）题目 38：One reason why some men may be unwilling to leave their jobs to look after their children is because the gains that could come with such a change are not obvious. Staying at home would in fact mean accepting a considerable drop in pay and in ________. The conventional notion that men are not as ________ as women may also lead men to experience a certain sense of resignation about their traditional place in society.
题目翻译：传统观念认为，男性不像女性那样具有什么特质？
答案：empathetic
定位：正文 E 段，后半部分
原文：The idea that men are naturally less empathetic also produces feelings of fatalism about their role.
译文：认为男性天生较缺乏共情能力的观念，也会使他们对自己的角色产生宿命感。

解析：not as ... as 与 less 构成同义比较，空格需要形容词 empathetic。

（3）题目 39：However, it is interesting to note that the majority of young men in the UK say that the statutory time permitted for ________ is inadequate. Influence is thus being exerted on the ________ to review the existing provision.
题目翻译：大多数英国年轻男性认为哪一种法定假期太短？
答案：paternity leave
定位：正文 G 段，中部
原文：three-quarters of young men tell pollsters that the amount of time fathers are allowed to take off work after a birth - paternity leave - is too short in Britain.
译文：四分之三的年轻男性告诉民意调查者，英国父亲在孩子出生后获准休假的时间——陪产假——太短。

解析：statutory time permitted 对应 amount of time fathers are allowed；原文明确把该制度命名为 paternity leave，因此填连续两词 paternity leave。

（4）题目 40：However, it is interesting to note that the majority of young men in the UK say that the statutory time permitted for ________ is inadequate. Influence is thus being exerted on the ________ to review the existing provision.
题目翻译：影响正施加于哪个主体，促使其审查现有规定？
答案：government
定位：正文 G 段，中后部
原文：The government is therefore proposing more equal policies on maternity/paternity leave, knowing that the pressure is still forwards rather than backwards.
译文：因此，政府正在提出更平等的产假和陪产假政策，因为它知道这种推动力仍在向前而不是倒退。

解析：Influence is being exerted on 对应 pressure；能够 review the existing provision 并提出政策的主体是 government，因此填 government。

questionExplanations.text:
（1）题目 37：One reason why some men may be unwilling to leave their jobs to look after their children is because the gains that could come with such a change are not obvious. Staying at home would in fact mean accepting a considerable drop in pay and in ________. The conventional notion that men are not as ________ as women may also lead men to experience a certain sense of resignation about their traditional place in society.
题目翻译：待在家照顾孩子会使收入和什么大幅下降？
答案：status
定位：正文 E 段，中部
原文：the gains in the parallel social revolution are harder for men to see, since it will involve them in losing status and income.
译文：男性较难看出这场平行社会变革的收益，因为它会使他们失去社会地位和收入。

解析：题干已用 pay 对应 income，另一个并列损失是 status，因此填 status。

（2）题目 38：One reason why some men may be unwilling to leave their jobs to look after their children is because the gains that could come with such a change are not obvious. Staying at home would in fact mean accepting a considerable drop in pay and in ________. The conventional notion that men are not as ________ as women may also lead men to experience a certain sense of resignation about their traditional place in society.
题目翻译：传统观念认为，男性不像女性那样具有什么特质？
答案：empathetic
定位：正文 E 段，后半部分
原文：The idea that men are naturally less empathetic also produces feelings of fatalism about their role.
译文：认为男性天生较缺乏共情能力的观念，也会使他们对自己的角色产生宿命感。

解析：not as ... as 与 less 构成同义比较，空格需要形容词 empathetic。

（3）题目 39：However, it is interesting to note that the majority of young men in the UK say that the statutory time permitted for ________ is inadequate. Influence is thus being exerted on the ________ to review the existing provision.
题目翻译：大多数英国年轻男性认为哪一种法定假期太短？
答案：paternity leave
定位：正文 G 段，中部
原文：three-quarters of young men tell pollsters that the amount of time fathers are allowed to take off work after a birth - paternity leave - is too short in Britain.
译文：四分之三的年轻男性告诉民意调查者，英国父亲在孩子出生后获准休假的时间——陪产假——太短。

解析：statutory time permitted 对应 amount of time fathers are allowed；原文明确把该制度命名为 paternity leave，因此填连续两词 paternity leave。

（4）题目 40：However, it is interesting to note that the majority of young men in the UK say that the statutory time permitted for ________ is inadequate. Influence is thus being exerted on the ________ to review the existing provision.
题目翻译：影响正施加于哪个主体，促使其审查现有规定？
答案：government
定位：正文 G 段，中后部
原文：The government is therefore proposing more equal policies on maternity/paternity leave, knowing that the pressure is still forwards rather than backwards.
译文：因此，政府正在提出更平等的产假和陪产假政策，因为它知道这种推动力仍在向前而不是倒退。

解析：Influence is being exerted on 对应 pressure；能够 review the existing provision 并提出政策的主体是 government，因此填 government。
